title: Add Andersen thermostat for Molecular Dynamics to ase.md
body:
DEV: add ase.md.andersen (Andersen thermostat)

TST:
- delete test_verlet.py, test_verlet_asap.py, test_langevin.py and test_langevin_asap.py; this cleans up
  - repetition of tests for varying pbc
  - repetition of tests for varying atomic systems
  - repetition of tests for varying calculators
  - several `QuasiNewton` optimizations after MD runs
  - rough temperature checks
- merge the essence of the deleted tests in test_verlet_thermostats.py; this includes tests for
  - conservation of total energy using `Verlet` (long traj)
  - reproduction of `Verlet` by `Langevin` and `Andersen` for switched off thermostats (short traj)
  - ability of thermostats (`Langevin`, `Andersen`) to achieve and conserve the target temperature on average (long traj)
  - thermalization by `MaxwellBoltzmannDistribution` to target temperature

DOC: update md.rst and releasenotes.rst

With the Andersen thermostat, temperature is imposed by random collisions with a heat bath.
author: jamsler

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
Hi @jamsler 

Thank you very much for this!

Should the temperature argument be called ``temperature_K`` for consistency with the other dynamics?

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: If I have understood you correctly, you are planning to change the unit for temperature to Kelvin on the long run and temperature_K is only a temporary compatibility measure? On the other hand, it is indeed more consistent to use temperature_K which also does not lead to misunderstandings. I changed it to temperature_K.

comments.body: I expect that we will keep the name ``temperature_K`` at least for quite a while.

The other dynamics use this ``xxx is None`` trick because a previous argument (the old temperature argument) had to be optional, but there is no need not to make ``andersen_prob`` a normal compulsory argument.

comments.author: schiotz

comments.body: In contrast to langevin.py, there is no temperature_eV argument in `__init__` of the Andersen class. So, the dictionary contains temperature_K instead.

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
I am not sure I follow you.

I was speaking about the ``fix-cm`` member of the dictionary, and whether the temperature should be called ``temperature_K`` in ``__init__`` (which I think it should, to be consistent among all the Dynamics).  Even the Berendsen dynamics got the ``temperature_K`` added although they already took a temperature in Kelvin, so all temperatures in all modules can be specified as ``temperature_K=300``, for example.

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: I know ;) I did not quite answer to the question of fix-cm. I just wanted to highlight, that there is an additional inconsistency between MD codes in the to_dict method regarding temperature.

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body: Ah!  That is a bug.  I'll look into that.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
> @askhl What is the use for the `todict` method? Should the keys not be identical to the arguments of the `__init__` method, i.e. `fix-cm` should be changed to `fixcm` here and in langevin.py ?

It's unfortunately not clear to me what the purpose of todict() on optimizers or MD is.

The purpose of todict() on `@jsonable` classes or objects which put `'ase_objtype'` into their dict is to support serialization via `ase.io.jsonio`.

MD and optimizers don't do this, nor do they attempt to dump all their attributes, which means they cannot be restored.

I can think of two things about optimizers which it would be beneficial to store: 1) the input parameters, 2) the full state (inputs, Atoms, calculator parameters, Hessian, ...), so as to resume an existing optimization.

As it is, my guess is that it's more of a logging thing ("who am I"), a better fit for `__str__()` or `__repr__()`.

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: It seems that the `Langevin` class is the only MD code that implements the `todict()` method. Since there is no essential reason to have it, I do not include the method in the `Andersen` class.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests changing the key `fix-cm` to `fixcm` in the `todict` method in both andersen.py and langevin.py.

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
I think this looks like it is ready to merge.

We have to address ``fix-cm`` when we hear from @askhl, but that is really not urgent and can just be fixed in another MR later.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: IMHO the conclusion is: Not worth worrying about todict() since there aren't established rules.  Since less is more, I would refrain from overriding or otherwise touching todict().

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Notes the `fix-cm` issue still needs to be addressed, implying a future code change is needed.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: "infinitely" improbable, but: `log(1 - y)` always works whereas log(y) could be log(0).

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: Very good point!

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a potential bug where `log(y)` could be `log(0)`, implying the code should use `log(1 - y)` instead.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Now the difficult question.

We have different MDs that work together with RATTLE constraints somehow, but I don't understand how that part works.

So: *If* this code were wrong in such a way that the RATTLE constraints were not handled correctly, then which test would fail?

In other words what behaviour is required  to work together with RATTLE constraints, and can we meaningfully distinguish between something that works and doesn't?

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: I can think of running an NVE ensemble with a constraint such as one of FixInternals. The energy average and the constraint should be conserved to pass the test. @schiotz, what do you think?

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
I think it would be important to test that thermalization does not break RATTLE.  I have no experience with rattle, I hardly even know how it works :-)

I guess a test would be to remove a significant fraction of the degrees of freedom (DOF) with RATTLE, then test that the kinetic energy ends up being as expected for the reduced number of DOFs.  And that the contraints are obeyed.

Does that make sense?

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: Okay, as far as I understand RATTLE in ASE the constraints are handled by `set_positions(..., apply_constraint=True)` and the `adjust_positions()` method of the corresponding constraint together with the recalculation of the real velocity. Currently, I do not see a problem with thermalization, as this only sets the initial momenta which are then modified by RATTLE in the MD class. However, I do not feel confident enough to design a fail-proof test at the moment, hence I suggest to open an issue 'add RATTLE test for MD'. I might come back to that issue later, when my projects (and experience) have grown the point of constrained MD.

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body: OK, I think this makes sense.

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: #759 was opened to address the missing test for RATTLE constraints in MD simulations.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Raises a concern about whether RATTLE constraints are handled correctly and asks what test would catch a failure, implying a test coverage gap that should be addressed.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
There are multiple loops over arrays filling with boltzmann_random, i.e., a mild case of duplication. To avoid repetition (and reduce risk of accidentally changing the order of random number generation) I suggest

```python
def boltzmann_random(self, width, shape):
    x = self.rng.random_sample(shape=shape)
    y = ...
    z = ...
    return z
```

This will also be much faster (array math vs python loops) in case that matters.

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: Good point, done.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests refactoring the duplicated loop logic into a shared `boltzmann_random` method with array math for performance.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: This can also be replaced with array expression `v[self.rng.random_sample(v.shape) <= v] = get_maxwell_....`

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: Done.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests replacing a loop with a vectorized array expression.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I have seen this snippet before in another test.  Please never duplicate any code.  Is there any other duplicate code I did not spot?

Can we port the test so it uses asap3 instead, and runs in less than one second?

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body:
The tests for Langevin, Andersen, Verlet and Verlet(asap3) are very similar. It should be possible to reduce code duplication by combining these tests into one test.

I am unfamiliar with asap3, are you @schiotz? It seems Langevin needs to broadcast its random numbers to work with asap3. What is required for Andersen to work with asap3?

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body:
Tests for Verlet and Langevin without asap3 were merged into one test_mds.py file which reduced code duplications. A test for Andersen was added to this file. Equivalence of Langevin and Andersen with Verlet for zero friction/andersen_prob is now tested using a very short trajectory.

For Verlet and Langevin there exist additional test files using asap3: test_verlet_asap.py and test_langevin_asap.py. These can be merged and extended by Andersen to a test file 'test_mds_asap.py' similarly to the tests without asap3.

If there is no reason to test the MD codes without asap3, then test_mds.py can be deleted and only test_mds_asap.py is kept.

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: I see, asap3 is an external calculator and MD package. I think we cannot port the test to use asap3 as this would leave untested ASE code.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests removing duplicate code from the test and porting it to use asap3 for faster execution.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Excellent, that can verified in a single MD step.  No need for a full propagation to verify that condition.

But does this mean that our Verlet implementation is redundant because it is a special case of Andersen?

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body: Technically it may be, but is it equally fast? Langevin is also a slow version of Verlet for friction=0.

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body:
I have compared the speed of Verlet, Langevin and Andersen using 100k steps for the setup used in test_mds.py. The relative speeds on my Macbook are Verlet : Langevin : Andersen = 1 : 1.17 : 1.23.
After around 20k steps the trajectories of Verlet, Langevin and Andersen differ slightly for numerical reasons. All three codes conserve total energy and thus generate an NVE ensemble. In my opinion the Verlet implementation is not redundant due to its significantly better performance.

So, apart from numerical differences after several thousand steps Andersen and Langevin do reproduce Verlet for andersen_prob/friction equal zero. This is now tested in test_mds.py using a very short trajectory.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests simplifying the test to use a single MD step rather than full propagation, and raises a design question about Verlet redundancy.

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
> I am unfamiliar with asap3, are you @schiotz? It seems Langevin needs to broadcast its random numbers to work with asap3. What is required for Andersen to work with asap3?

I am the main asap maintainer.  The broadcasting in Langevin is not for asap, it is for gpaw: in parallel gpaw calculations it is essential that the atoms maintain the same positions on all MPI tasks, that is what the broadcast is used for and something similar should be done for Andersen thermalization.

Asap has the atoms distributed between MPI tasks, so there the random numbers should be independent.  On the other hand, the atoms migrate when forces are calculated, so all per-atom data should be on the atoms when forces are calculated.  Here that is only the velocities, which are kept on the atoms in Verlet for this reason.  I'll try to use Andersen with asap and see if it works.  For langevin, a special langevin class is used in asap, it is derived from ase.md.langevin and just defines a helper method that binds the temporary arrays to the atoms object so they get migrated along other data, but I do not foresee that to be necessary for Andersen.

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body:
Hi @schiotz, based on your comment I have adapted the Andersen code so that it should be compatible with asap and gpaw. In detail, random per-atom variables are now stored as attributes and broadcasted via the communicator:
- self.random_com_velocity  # added to all atoms if self.fix_com
- self.random_velocity      # added to some atoms if the per-atom
- self.andersen_chance      # andersen_chance <= andersen_prob

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Explains that broadcasting is needed for parallel GPAW calculations and implies similar broadcasting logic should be added to the Andersen thermostat.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Instead of communicator being None, you can use ase.parallel.SerialCommunicator().  That one has dummy implementations of broadcast etc., so the if-statements will be unnecessary (in multiple places)

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: If I understand ase.parallel correctly, then I think that `communicator=ase.parallel.world` will assign the correct communicator (dummy or whatever). So, I can remove the if statement. By the way: this if statement is also found in langevin.py. I removed it now.

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body:
I noticed that the DOC strings in langevin.py (and andersen.py) tell the user to set the communicator to None to disable communication. So, I add `if communicator is None: communicator = DummyMPI()`.

Btw, I could not find `ase.parallel.SerialCommunicator()`, I assume you meant `DummyMPI()`.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests replacing `None` communicator checks with `ase.parallel.SerialCommunicator()` to eliminate multiple if-statements.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
This is a copy from langevin.

We should make use of programming constructs like functions, methods, shared superclasses, or object composition so the computer takes care of the repetition instead of humans needing to know about the duplication and remember to update the same thing in multiple places.

Can the duplication be eliminated?

If there was any other duplication that I didn't spot (yet), then the same comment applies.

I furthermore spotted a duplicated `_get_com_velocity()` (used by Langevin and Andersen) and moved it to the super class.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:

Please eliminate duplication by having either 1) shortcut methods to build MD objects, or 2) pass `**kwargs`, etc.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests eliminating 4-fold parameter duplication in the test file using shortcut methods or `**kwargs`.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
(Why are we deleting the reference?)

The two tests look alike.  It would be good to replace them via common functions, fixtures, or parametrization, so it's easy to see (without prior knowledge of all the files) that they belong together and what their exact differences are.

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body:
No idea, the reference was deleted in the old tests. Now, I removed the deletion.

The major differences between the two tests are
- the calculator (asap3.EMT vs. TestPotential)
- the atomic system
- the use of pbc
- the specific tests (temperature ramping, reproduction of Verlet by Langevin and Andersen with zero thermostat, conservation of total energy, average temperature, ...)

I think this is it for now. Perhaps one could concatenate the two files into one file to stress that they belong together.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Questions deletion of a reference and requests the two similar tests be unified via common functions, fixtures, or parametrization.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Back in the days this test was probably fully random and would fail if temperature fell outside the interval.

Now we control the seed centrally (with rng) so we won't get random failures.  Hence, let's tighten the criterion so it's within perhaps 300 +/- 50 K (I don't know the actual numbers).

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: Actually, the temperature fluctuates heavily. The thermostats conserve temperature only on average over long trajectories. Here we can detect problems in the units or errors with similar orders of magnitude (see comment in the code).

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: OK, I see.  But if we can't verify the temperature after 10000 steps, shouldn't we just delete it?  I mean either it tests 10000 steps *and* we gain a verifiable quantitative agreement, *or* we simply delete the test (less is more) and rely on the one using asap3.

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body:
Right, it may help to summarize what we want to test:
- conservation of total energy using `Verlet` (long traj)
- reproduction of `Verlet` by `Langevin` and `Andersen` for switched off thermostats (short traj)
- thermalization by `MaxwellBoltzmannDistribution` to target temperature
- ability of thermostats to conserve temperature on average (long traj)

Anything else may probably be deleted, e.g.:
- repetition of tests for varying pbc
- repetition of tests for varying atomic systems
- repetition of tests for varying calculators
- several `QuasiNewton` optimizations after MD runs in test_mds.py
- rough temperature checks in test_mds.py

comments.author: jamsler
comments.body: I have merged the tests according to the above listed summary.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests tightening the temperature test criterion (e.g., 300 ± 50 K) since random failures are no longer a concern with a seeded RNG.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I now realize: We should try to avoid having many methods on Atoms that grow in different "directions".  The atoms.py change should really be expressed via a keyword in `atoms.center()`, maybe atoms.center(about='cou') (meaning center of unit cell) following an existing convention from atoms.rotate().

But upon looking more closely, atoms.center() has some old behaviours wrt. periodicity and cell vector definitions which make it slightly non-straightforward.  I might try to improve that.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests replacing the atoms.py change with a keyword on `atoms.center()` instead of adding a new method, indicating a concrete refactoring request.
